newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU commission probes Alitalia aid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU commission probes Alitalia aid.

text.p: The European Commission opened a state aid probe into planned payments of 1.5 trillion lire ($990 million) to Italian airline Alitalia, an EU source said on Wednesday.
The decision, which passed without discussion at Wednesday's weekly Commission meeting, begins an investigation into the struggling carrier which may take officials several months.

Wednesday's move brings Alitalia into a long line of Commission-investigated aid cases which includes state-owned carriers such as Spain's Iberia, Air France, Greece's Olympic Airways, Ireland's Aer Lingus, and TAP Air Portugal.
In the end, the Commission has approved all previous cases but with conditions.
"The Italians will argue that in their opinion, it's not a state aid at all," said one senior Commission official, indicating that this might be why the airline had not been looked at earlier.
"They may have received aid before but there's no way the Commission could have known unless it had been alerted by a competitor or by other means," the official said.
"I do not know whether the Italians have finished designing their overall plan yet. There's no reason to assume this will be a quick process," the official added.
The plan for a 1.5 trillion lire capital increase for the airline was approved by industrial state holding company IRI, Alitalia's majority shareholder, in July.
Alitalia has said the money constitutes a capital injection that any investor would make.
Last week, rival airline British Airways said it would complain to the Commission over what it says is unfair aid.
